verdict_note: From reading only: no build, no test, no GUI. Line anchors are crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layer_records.rs at 95460d11 unless a file is named. The central mechanism holds. structure_step (:111-117) keeps the pre-step snapshot, runs the step, and prune_removed (:122-141) computes removed = layers before minus layers after. It writes the pruned raster, vector and text entries through Run::entries_into_newest_step (harness-core harness.rs:1535). That call groups them with the step (:1545-1606): undo and redo swap whole entries (history_step/swap_entry), and a refused write puts the written entries back and rolls the step back with no redo entry. Nested groups (board_commit's catalog_step) replay through group_step. The rollbacks after the step in native_redraw (instance.rs:1249) and duplicate_instances (component.rs:925) now undo the step and its prune together. Every harness-view site that the lane's V4-06 regex finds goes through the prune. delete_layer's old helpers are gone, and the board's own delete_node pre-drop is idempotent with the prune. No path, story or paint-style false negative was found in the token scan for any current producer. One HIGH data-loss defect blocks: drop_stories, now run for every removed text layer and dropped text binding, deletes named and imported type styles without the Q1 scan (F1). F2 (layer-removing siblings outside structure_step) and F3 (the tests prove removal only, never preservation) are medium. F4 (scan cost, glued-reference misses, no integrity backstop) is also medium. F5-F8 are low.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. No session entry encodes ids as base64 or compressed (session entries are raw bytes; zstd applies to assets only). findings.where: :69-80 id_tokens; :179-204 elsewhere and referenced(), called up to three times per prune (:282, :336, :373); id_tokens over the vector and text entries (:215, :356); :289 post-prune check
findings.what: Each referenced() call re-serializes the after document and the receipt to JSON. It then collects every id-shaped token of every session document entry into a BTreeSet<String>, one allocation per distinct token, and tests membership. This runs up to three times per prune, on every structure step that removes a layer and names a candidate, with no self.cancel check. Matching is token equality, so a reference glued to id bytes ('SVPT-..._x', 'x-SVPT-...') is not found, and the record is pruned while still referenced. The post-prune VectorEntry::decode against after (:289) checks path format, live shapes and records filtered to present layers. It does not check that every path id after names still resolves, so such a miss goes uncaught.
findings.scenario: In a layout document near the package entry limits, each Delete holds the UI thread for three serializations and three full-session scans and builds a token set as large as every id in every entry, and cancel is ignored. A future producer that keys a record by '{path_id}_width' would lose the path silently.
findings.fix: Make one pass per prune: serialize the document and the receipt once, and search all parts for the union of candidate ids as substrings (aho-corasick or memchr::memmem). Any occurrence keeps the id, which is conservative and allocation-free. Check self.cancel between parts. After pruning, require that every path id named by after's payloads, live shapes, boolean groups, meshes, path and area texts and brush art, and by layout graphic frames, resolves in the pruned entry. If one does not, keep those paths.
findings.test: (1) A candidate id that occurs only glued to id bytes in an entry the scan reads (a design-state or receipt fixture) stays. (2) A large-session delete, with time and allocation bounds asserted against a fixed budget. (3) Cancel set before the prune: nothing is pruned and the step stays consistent (per the answer to lead question 3).

findings.certainty: READ; not run. No public path that commits a layer removal without pushing a history step was found; restructure_inner pushes only when changed and an inverse exists (harness.rs:1460-1466).
findings.severity: low (latent: a prune joined to the wrong step, and a false rollback message)
findings.what: prune_removed groups its entries into whatever step is newest, without checking that the structure step pushed it. If a step removes layers without pushing a history step, the prune entries join the previous, unrelated step. A refused write then rolls that unrelated step back (rollback_newest_step). With an empty undo stack the write is refused nothing_to_undo, and the message says the step was rolled back although it stays committed.
findings.fix: Record the undo depth before the step and group only when the depth grew by one. Otherwise refuse with a typed code (for example layer_records_no_step) without touching older steps.
findings.test: A harness-view unit test with a step closure that commits a delete but pushes no history step: no prune write, and the older step stays intact.

answers.token_scan_misses: Exact token equality over runs of [A-Za-z0-9_-] with a four-capital prefix. Numeric, case and escaping: ids are DomainId strings compared byte-exactly everywhere, and no case-insensitive id compare exists. JSON escapes (backslash-quote, slashes, colons) split runs correctly. Binary or base64: session document entries are raw bytes (JSON here), and zstd applies to assets only, so no reference is encoded. Binary entries can only add false positives, which keep more. Miss class: a reference glued to id bytes (F4). No current producer found. Not scanned at all: preserved unknown package entries, import entries other than the receipt, and in-memory editor state. History needs no scan, because every prune restore is a whole-entry swap inside the step's group.
answers.data_loss_paths: Paths: the consumers are layer payloads, live shapes, boolean fill geometry, mesh source, path and area texts, brush art, width profiles (folded into path records at decode), and longdoc graphic-frame Path shapes. Longdoc frames are missing from the lane's consumer list but covered, because layout_records is scanned. No concrete false negative found. Stories: kept when named anywhere. Side rows keyed by text_id pin a story forever (F1). Type styles: dropped without the scan, which is data loss (F1). Paint styles: own appearance styles only, scanned; graphic styles kept by publish key. Clipboard: none persisted and none in memory (the clipboard menu rows are pending). Symbols and libraries: none. Linked and placed documents: placed sources are kept. Design states and layout records: scanned, not pruned. Masks: a clip or mask whose source left is dropped, and its targets lose it (approved; lead question 2). Text on a path or in an area is deleted with its carrier (lead question 2).
answers.outside_step_undo_redo: Every prune write goes through entries_into_newest_step into the step's group. Undo swaps the entries back and then reverses the step; redo re-applies both. Callers' existing out-of-history writes (place_text, live text, point/area conversions, replace_with_pieces store_entry, fig redraw) land before the step. The group's restore holds the post-write bytes, which is consistent with swap semantics. Nothing is pruned outside a step.
answers.refused_write: Yes, for a refused prune write: group_entries_with_newest puts the written entries back and calls rollback_newest_step (no redo entry); prune_removed returns Err; place.rs maps it to the op's typed refusal. A failed rollback is the known 'atomic multi-entry history step' gap. Assumption that the newest step is this step: F6. A prune that cannot be computed does not roll back (F5).
answers.bounded_cancel: Bounded only by package and entry limits. Up to three full-session scans and serializations per prune, with no cancel check (F4). pruned_vector also decodes the vector entry twice and re-serializes it up to three times on every vector-layer delete, because the layer's own paths always name a candidate.
answers.double_prune: None harmful. delete_layer's old helpers are removed. Board delete_node drops its binding and story inside board_commit's step, and the prune then takes only the node's paths. native_redraw's drop_deleted_copies runs before the step without the Q1 scan (the approved MAX_PATHS deviation; lead question 6). container_records_into_step (artboard and page nodes) is separate.
answers.skipped_structure_paths: Inside harness-view, every regex hit is fixed. Outside the regex: Viewer::delete_page, layout_commit (smart reflow, layout page delete) and Run::play_action restructure (batch) (F2).
answers.tests: They prove each family's removal, same-step undo with byte-identical restore (tests 3-6), redo, save/reopen and the reused-id case. They do not prove preservation, the Q1 keep branch, a refused-write rollback, the layout path, plain text, or raster rows through other steps (F3).
